reader.title: Killing of an unnamed Black man near Australia Landing (1888)
bases: A single white man, Robert Taylor, is reported to have shot and killed one Black man in a personal confrontation, with no mob, band or officers involved (A2, A3).
The only reports are two printings of one Memphis dispatch (A2, A3); the fuller wire and Memphis Avalanche accounts of the lynching on the same plantations do not mention the shooting (A1, A4).

summary.text: The killing of an unnamed Black man near Australia Landing was a fatal shooting in March 1888 on the Sledge and Mason plantations, a few miles below Australia Landing, in which Robert Taylor, a white man, shot and killed a Black man who, according to the only report, had attempted to strike him.
The shooting reached the press only as a single sentence in a Memphis dispatch that was mainly about a lynching on the same plantations.

According to a Memphis dispatch of Thursday, news had arrived that day from the Sledge and Mason plantations of "a killing and lynching which occurred there on Saturday last," which would place the shooting on March 24, 1888.
The dispatch said that Robert Taylor, "a white man, shot and killed a negro who attempted to strike him."
It did not name the dead man or say what led to the confrontation, and the account of the attempted blow is the only version given.

The same dispatch went on to describe a separate killing, in which a Black man who had cut "a very popular negro" with a razor during a game was dragged to a levee and hanged by "men of his own race."
No report of an arrest, inquest or legal proceeding against Taylor appears in the coverage.

The item ran in the Semi-weekly South Kentuckian of Hopkinsville, Kentucky, on March 30, 1888, and in the Yorkville Enquirer of South Carolina on April 4, where it appeared among miscellaneous items in a "Scraps and Facts" column.

Both versions gave the shooting a single sentence without comment and devoted the rest of the item to the lynching; they differed only in that the Yorkville text dated the events and called the game "cards" rather than "craps."
Neither paper questioned the claim that the dead man had tried to strike Taylor, and neither followed up on the shooting.

accounts.label: Memphis dispatch
accounts.gist: News reaching Memphis from the Sledge and Mason plantations said Robert Taylor, a white man, shot and killed a negro who attempted to strike him; the same dispatch reported a separate lynching of a Black man by Black men.

framing.detail: The Kentucky and South Carolina papers ran the Memphis item as filler (A3 in its 'Scraps and Facts' column), giving the shooting one sentence and the dead man's attempted blow as its only explanation, ahead of the lynching story.

versions.value: 'on Saturday last' before a Thursday (March 29) dispatch, i.e. March 24

conflicts.note: Not a contradiction; only A3 dates the events. A4, about the lynching only, places the ball 'about the middle of last week', which may not fit 'Saturday last', but it does not mention the shooting.
Concerns the separate lynching in the same dispatch, not the shooting.
